claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a relatively uniform solid-solution microstructure.
The untreated baseline coating lacks promoted Cu segregation and is coarser than the anticipated sliding-induced surface layer.
A suitable post-deposition heat treatment will produce moderate Cu segregation at grain boundaries without excessive grain coarsening.
At 500–700 °C, diffusion and dynamic recrystallization are active during sliding of the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Using an inert or controlled atmosphere minimizes oxidation and oxide-film formation during sliding.
Controlled Cu segregation produces Cu-rich nanoscale precipitates at grain boundaries.
High-temperature sliding of the Cu-segregated coating produces an ultra-nanocrystalline, Cu-rich surface glaze.
Cu segregation reduces local lattice cohesion.
Segregated Cu or Cu-rich precipitates pin dislocations.
The effects of Cu segregation under high-temperature sliding lead to dynamic recrystallization and surface grain refinement.
The ultra-nanocrystalline surface layer changes deformation from localized shear to more homogeneous plastic flow.
More homogeneous plastic flow suppresses localized shear and crack initiation.
Formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer reduces wear.
The heat-treated coating will have a lower friction coefficient than the as-deposited coating.
The heat-treated coating will have a lower wear rate than the as-deposited coating.
Excessive heat treatment causing over-segregation or grain coarsening may eliminate the predicted benefits.
Severely oxidative operating conditions may cause behavior to deviate from the predictions obtained under inert conditions.

The hypothesis is falsified if treatment fails to produce a statistically significant reduction in wear rate and friction, or if it fails to produce the expected Cu-rich nanocrystalline layer and deformation-mode shift.
